description: Ultra-fast setting and curing hydraulic binder for stopping water leaks
whereToUse: For instant stopping of water leaks, even water under pressure.
Stopping water leaks in basements, subways and below grade structures in general.
Stopping water leaks in tanks above ground.
Waterproof sealing of rigid joints between walls and floor slabs.
Waterproof sealing of cracks and holes.
notFor: Do not add lime, cement or gypsum to Lamposilex.
Do not leave drums of Lamposilex exposed to sunlight before using.

standards.value: suitable for use in potable water. Certified to AS/NZS 4020:2018.
The product complies with the conditions of Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) N° 1907/2006 (REACH) - All. XVII, item 47.

technicalData.label: Mix ratio by volume
technicalData.value: 2.5 parts by Lamposilex to 1 part water

technicalData.label: The minimum external sizes
technicalData.value: must be about 2 cm in width and 2 cm in depth

consumption.basis: per one-dm³ (cubic decimetre) of cavity volume filled
consumption.quote: 1.8 kg of Lamposilex will fill a one-dm³ cavity.

mixing: While stirring, pour 1 kg of Lamposilex into a container holding 280 g of water and mix manually with trowel to obtain a smooth mix with no lumps. For dosing by volume, mix 2.5 parts Lamposilex with 1 part water.
storage: Store the product in a dry place indoor for 12 months.
notes: Consumption is given only per cavity volume (1.8 kg per dm³); the sheet gives no per-m2 or per-linear-metre figure. There are no coats or layer thicknesses for this product; the only dimensional requirement is the minimum prepared crack/hole size (about 2 cm wide and 2 cm deep), recorded as a technicalData row taken from the body text. Setting time is described as about one and a half minutes at +20°C while pot life is given as approx. 1 minute. The recommendations refer to 'drums of Lamposilex' but the packaging is a box with 4 bags of 5 kg. The table row for mix ratio by volume reads '2.5 parts by Lamposilex' (sic). Strength rows are sub-rows of the table; the values recorded keep the 'after ...' sub-row label with its figure. EN 196/1 appears only as the test method for the strength values, so it is not listed under standards. This is the Mapei Australia edition of the sheet.
